correctness.rationale: Degree-four lower bound forces every minimum set to be a closed neighborhood with precisely one missing neighbor. This yields exactly the 3m cyclic sets after normalization. Direct forcing-front induction proves propagation times n-2 and n-1. Four-set intersection determines the complete 9m-edge reconfiguration adjacency table. A 1-Lipschitz center-coordinate map yields eccentricity at least n for all states; consecutive 3-anchor intervals on the A-cycle yield the matching upper bound. Distinct Python and C++ source programs independently reproduce finite enumerations and BFS results.

value.rationale: The square of an even cycle is the canonical polyhedral antiprism family. The theorem characterizes not only the minimum zero-forcing budget but every optimal placement, its propagation speed, and exact one-token reconfiguration geometry. It provides an infinite, bounded-degree, connected and nonregular self-centered reconfiguration family with linear diameter, showing a structural feature that neither mere counting nor generic bounds supply; both rapid propagation and mobility among optimal placements matter in zero-forcing network control.
